from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs');p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)

(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join('\\n===== PAGE '+str(i+1)+' =====\\n'+t for i,t in enumerate(texts)))

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import math
for steps in (1000,10000,100000):
 cumulative=[0.,0.]
 policy=[.5,.5]
 achieved=0.
 for t in range(steps):
  reward=(1.,0.) if t%2==0 else (0.,.5)
  value=sum(policy[a]*reward[a] for a in range(2))
  achieved+=value
  for a in range(2):
   cumulative[a]+=max(0.,reward[a]-value)
  total=sum(cumulative)
  policy=[x/total for x in cumulative] if total else [.5,.5]
 regret=steps/2-achieved
 claimed_bound=2*math.sqrt(2*steps)
 print(f'T={steps}: Algorithm 1 regret={regret:.3f}, regret/T={regret/steps:.5f}, stated regret-matching bound={claimed_bound:.3f}, final policy={policy}')
PY"

strengths: The progression from requesting help to context-dependent cautious actions and sequential driving provides an interpretable investigation of learned caution. Researchers studying uncertainty and robust decision-making have an identifiable reason to read this work.

The experiments demonstrate meaningful behavioral effects of risk aversion, including increased help-seeking on unfamiliar images and reduced driving speed and collisions. Comparing single-image and all-images objectives reveals an informative dependence on how robustness is defined.

Theorem 1 provides a useful reduction from state-local regret to policy regret through discounted occupancy measures. The manuscript also explicitly acknowledges its restrictions to known transitions, tabular planning, and expensive policy evaluation.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the mismatch between Algorithm 1 and the theoretical guarantees. The pseudocode accumulates positive instantaneous regrets, rather than applying regret matching to cumulative signed regrets. This distinction is substantive: with alternating two-action reward vectors (1,0) and (0,1/2), the printed update can incur linear regret. Identify the update actually used in the experiments, correct the algorithm description, and revalidate results if necessary. The guarantees currently do not justify Algorithm 1 as written.

Necessary: Correct the theoretical presentation. Appendix C, equations (11)–(13), reverses the relevant probability inequalities and omits the negative sign in the exponential tail bound; the martingale argument also needs explicit conditioning on the sampling history. These appear repairable. Separately, Theorem 3 bounds the best or uniformly sampled iterate, whereas the following paragraph claims convergence of the policy sequence and the experiments return the last iterate. State precisely which conclusions are established.

Necessary: Reconcile the empirical reporting and make the performance costs prominent. Section 4 reports less than 2% help-seeking on familiar images, but Table 2 gives 2.83% for the strongest single-image policy. More substantially, Table 4 reports familiar-image accuracy of 84.13% for 1-of-20 versus 99.28% for 10-of-10 when help is available. These substantial tradeoffs should accompany the reported gains in caution.

Necessary: Qualify inaccurate exclusions in the related-work discussion. POMDPs do not necessarily contain only aleatoric uncertainty or uncertainty that further observations can resolve; unknown fixed parameters can be represented as latent variables. CMDPs also need not enumerate safe states or actions. Explain the particular information and feedback assumptions distinguishing this work without making categorical claims about these frameworks.

Optional: Strengthen the interpretation of the driving results with collision rates per distance and a speed-matched baseline. Figure 4’s strongest policy moves very little, so reduced collision frequency alone does not isolate obstacle-aware planning from reduced exposure. Independent ensemble repetitions would also complement the current repetitions, which reshuffle one fixed ensemble. Larger benchmarks or state-of-the-art performance are not prerequisites for accepting this proof of concept.
